world_map.note: 40 cities: 20 USA, 20 USSR. Cities are independent targets with no adjacency. Population in millions.

icbm_stockpile.note: ICBM count. USA starts with 1000, USSR starts with 1200.

slbm_stockpile.note: SLBM count. USA starts with 600, USSR starts with 500.

bomber_stockpile.note: Bomber count. USA starts with 200, USSR starts with 150.

abm_stockpile.note: ABM interceptor count. Both sides start with 100.

surviving_population.note: Surviving population in millions. Starts at sum of own city populations. Decremented as cities are destroyed.

targeting_orders.note: Secret targeting assignments. Each entry assigns a missile to an enemy city. Hidden until launch phase resolution.

defense_orders.note: Secret ABM deployment assignments. Each entry assigns interceptors to defend a friendly city. Hidden until resolution.

missile.note: Nuclear delivery systems. Warheads = number of independent targets. Yield = destruction rating per warhead.

interceptor.note: ABM interceptors. Each has 30% chance to destroy one incoming warhead.

phases.name: defcon_5_diplomacy
phases.note: Both players simultaneously declare posture: escalate, hold, or negotiate. Two negotiates = game ends in peace (draw). Two escalates = skip to DEFCON 1.

phases.name: abm_deployment
phases.note: Both players secretly allocate ABM interceptors to their own cities. Limited stockpile forces hard choices.

phases.name: targeting
phases.note: Both players secretly assign missiles to enemy cities. Each missile targets one city. Sealed orders — opponent cannot see targeting until launch.

phases.name: launch
phases.note: Both players simultaneously confirm launch or stand down. Commit-reveal ensures neither can react to the other's decision. Both launch = mutual exchange. One launches = first strike. Neither launches = de-escalation.

phases.name: resolution
phases.note: Server resolves all strikes simultaneously. For each incoming missile: ABM intercept roll (30% per interceptor assigned to target city). Surviving warheads destroy proportional population. Bombers can be recalled if only one side launched.

phases.name: assessment
phases.note: Calculate surviving population per side. If both below survival threshold (25% of starting population): mutual destruction — draw. Otherwise: side with more surviving population wins.

missile_allocation.definition: Each missile targets exactly one enemy city

abm_defense.definition: ABM interceptors defend own cities against incoming warheads

intercept_resolution.definition: Each interceptor has 30% chance to destroy one incoming warhead
intercept_resolution.server_resolves: for each interceptor: roll d100, if <= 30 then warhead destroyed

city_destruction.definition: Surviving warheads destroy population proportional to yield

bomber_recall.definition: Bombers can be recalled if player did not launch
bomber_recall.constraint: only if player chose stand_down in launch phase

mutual_destruction.definition: If both sides fall below 25% surviving population, the game is a draw
mutual_destruction.effect: A strange game. The only winning move is not to play.

first_strike.definition: If only one side launches, defending side's bombers are destroyed on the ground
first_strike.effect: defender loses all bomber_stockpile; only ICBMs and SLBMs on alert can retaliate

negotiation.definition: If both players choose negotiate in diplomacy phase, game ends peacefully

end_conditions.condition: both players chose negotiate in defcon_5_diplomacy phase
end_conditions.name: peace

end_conditions.condition: both players surviving_population below 25% of starting
end_conditions.name: mutual_destruction

end_conditions.condition: opponent surviving_population below 25% and own above 25%
end_conditions.name: strategic_victory

end_conditions.condition: both players chose stand_down in launch phase
end_conditions.name: de_escalation
